q: Can buyers call Samalaju aluminium low carbon because the smelters run on hydropower?
title: Samalaju hydro aluminium: what you can claim
short: For the product footprint, yes if the smelter shows its electricity really comes from hydropower and gives a cradle to gate figure that includes alumina. For CBAM it changes nothing: electricity is not charged for aluminium, so the certificates depend on anode and perfluorocarbon emissions only.
audience: Buyers of Malaysian primary aluminium and extruders using Samalaju ingot or billet

p: Smelting electricity is the biggest part of primary aluminium's footprint, so a smelter supplied by hydropower plants can show a much lower cradle to gate figure than one on a coal grid.

ul: The power supply contract or plant link that shows where the electricity comes from.
A cradle to gate figure per tonne that includes the alumina, which is imported and often made with coal or oil.
Anode and perfluorocarbon emissions, which count under CBAM.

p: Do not call the metal zero carbon. Anodes, perfluorocarbons, alumina and casting fuel still emit.

senseible: Senseible reads anode, fuel and electricity invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so a buyer can see which inputs sit behind each figure. Factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.
